newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Armed Belgian police swoop on suspected bandits.
newsitem.headline: Armed Belgian police swoop on suspected bandits.

text.p: Armed Belgian police and gendarmes, in a coordinated action, swooped before dawn on Monday on suspected members of a gang that has mounted a series of violent robberies across the country in the past year.
Four people were arrested in the raids on houses in five locations in central and southern Belgium.

"The operation started at five o'clock. We were able to arrest four people in connection with robberies and attacks on security vans," Philippe Warny, chief of police in the Namur region, told reporters.
"We took all the necessary precautions," he said, adding that psychiatrists and counsellors had gone in after the police because there were children in some of the houses.
The raids on Monday followed others earlier this month and in January in which police seized quantities of arms, ammunition, explosives, radio scanners and cash.

In an operation two weeks ago police confiscated 90 assault and hunting rifles, 4,000 rounds of ammunition, a kilogramme of explosives, scanners for monitoring police frequencies and two million francs ($59,000) in cash.

In mid-January police seized assault rifles, machine guns, shotguns, pistols, knives, masks, hundreds of kilos of ammunition and explosives in a raid on an isolated farmhouse near the central town of Nivelles.
There have been a series of violent attacks on security vans over the past year all over Belgium in which at least one person has been killed and several injured.

Last July, after a particularly bloody string of attacks, all movement of money in security vans was briefly suspended causing a massive build-up of cash at stores and supermarkets and causing a security crisis of its own.

There have also been a series of attacks on hole-in-the-wall cash dispensers with the would-be thieves using explosives in attempts to extract if not open the money machines -- the most recent having taken place just two weeks ago.
In one case, there was a shoot-out with police. The thieves escaped.
It is not clear how much money the various attacks have netted the bandits.
